tracks.narration: What load pulls the most power out of a source?
A real source has an internal resistance R sub s. The current through any load R sub L equals V sub s divided by R sub s plus R sub L. The power delivered into the load is I squared times R sub L.

Sweep the load from very small to very large. With a tiny load, the current is huge but the load voltage is nearly zero — almost no power. With a huge load, the voltage is full but the current is nearly zero — also almost no power. The peak sits in the middle.

At the peak the load equals R sub s, and the delivered power is V sub s squared over four R sub s. Half the source energy goes to the load, half is wasted in R sub s — fifty percent efficiency at maximum power transfer.
Match the load when you want maximum power — useful for antennas and signal receivers, wasteful for power distribution.
